question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}9 & 12 \\ 12 & 16\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}25 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} & -\frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5} & \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ what is the second column of $U?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ and ${\sigma }_{i}\ne 0,$ then the $i$th column of $U$ can be found as

$$
{u}_{i}=\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{i}}A{v}_{i},
$$

 

where ${u}_{i}$ and ${v}_{i}$ are the $i$th columns of the orthogonal matrices $U$ and $V,$ respectively.  

From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that the singular values are ${\sigma }_{1}=\sqrt{10}$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the first column of $U$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}9 & 12 \\ 12 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Since the second singular value is ${\sigma }_{2}=0$, we can't use the same formula to find the second column of $U.$ But we know that $U$ must be orthogonal. Hence, we must find a vector

$$
{u}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

such that 

$$
{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,‖{u}_{2}‖=1.
$$

 

Solving ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0,$ which is equivalent to

$$
\frac{3}{5}{x}_{1}+\frac{4}{5}{x}_{2}=0,
$$

we get a nonzero solution $[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Normalizing this vector, we finally obtain the  second column of $U:$

$$
{u}_{2}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]
$$
